title: Mini-wave coalescer and attention-slot multiplexing for tail resilience
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Goal: Reduce end-to-end P99 latency for mixed short/long conversational workloads by improving continuous-batching admission and matching attention compute to kernel capabilities. Approach combines a deterministic micro-wave coalescer (merge near-simultaneous prefill requests into small waves sized to target kernel memory occupancy), attention-slot multiplexing (pack attention compute across compatible requests to improve kernel utilization), and a lightweight tail-probing detector that triggers preferential scheduling for likely stragglers. This ticket covers design, prototype integration in the serving runtime, perf validation, and a canary rollout plan.
background: Current continuous-batching suffers from long tails when small, latency-sensitive requests interleave with bulky long-prefill requests. Existing admission heuristics bias throughput but under-serve mixed PLG traffic where short requests dominate user-perceived latency. Kernel selection currently chooses implementations based on static shape tables which miss transient skews; we need dynamic mapping combined with admission policies to preserve p99 SLOs without sacrificing throughput.
acceptance_criteria: P99 latency under mixed chat-mix workload reduced by >=25% compared to baseline (measured on runtime-1.21 kernel defaults)
Throughput regression <=5% on end-to-end QPS for the same hardware profile
No functional regressions in decoding correctness or token order (existing unit+integration tests pass)
Instrumentation added: per-wave size distribution, kernel-match counts, tail-probe triggers, and p50/p95/p99 per-route
Canary rollout plan documented and validated with chaos tests (simulate node evictions and KV-cache misses)
design_decisions: Use deterministic micro-waves sized to the L2 working set of the chosen kernel to avoid variable kernel thrashing
Implement attention-slot multiplexing as an additional packing step after admission that only merges requests with compatible sequence lengths and same model variant to avoid KV cache invalidations
Tail-probe uses an EWMA-based per-route latency predictor plus a lightweight speculative decode for top-1 token to detect stragglers; speculative work is cancelable and metered
Kernel-match table will be extended with recent telemetry: last-10s average occupancy and p99 to pick between quantized/FP16 kernels per-wave
Priority tagging: P0 customers get warm-path reservations (hot slots) to avoid coalescing when latency-critical; default PLG traffic uses coalescer
tradeoffs_and_risks: Micro-wave coalescing can increase headroom latency for extremely bursty, heterogeneous workloads; mitigated via priority tags and per-route opt-out
Attention-slot multiplexing adds packing CPU overhead; may slightly increase scheduling jitter on very high QPS nodes
Speculative tail-probing consumes extra cycles for a fraction of requests; we cap total speculative work per-GPU to limit cost impact
Dynamic kernel selection based on short-term telemetry may oscillate; use hysteresis and cooldown windows to avoid thrashing

benchmarks_and_results: Baseline (runtime-1.21, kernel-default): chat-mix-2026-02 on p4d: p50=45ms, p95=120ms, p99=320ms, throughput=1.0x
Prototype v0 (coalescer only): p50=47ms, p95=110ms, p99=255ms, throughput=0.99x
Prototype v1 (coalescer + attention multiplex): p50=46ms, p95=105ms, p99=230ms, throughput=1.02x
Add tail-probe + kernel telemetry: p99=210ms, throughput=1.06x (observed ~6% throughput improvement due to better kernel packing)
Note: numbers measured on mixed-tenant testbed with synthetic distribution (40% short <16 tokens, 40% medium 64-128 tokens, 20% long >256 tokens)
review_feedback: Leah O'Connor (SRE): asked for rate-limited speculative work and per-GPU caps to avoid overload; implemented cap=5% of compute window
Diego Rivera (Perf): requested cooldown window of 10s before switching kernel for a given wave to reduce oscillation; added hysteresis to selector
Marcus Chen (Owner): suggested adding per-route opt-out to Console and feature-flag the attention multiplexing for gradual rollout

rollout_plan: Gate behind feature flag 'mini_wave_v1' and run on 10% of serving traffic for one week
Monitor p50/p95/p99 per-route and abort if any route sees >15% regression in p50 or >5% regression in throughput
Gradually increase to 50% after 2 stable days, then 100% if no regressions and mean cost/unit unchanged
Post-rollout: run long-tail regression evals and document kernel-match histograms in runtime release notes
